raw_response:
I've been farming this 7.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. At 58, I know every patch of this land — where it stays wet after rain, where the soil is thinner. My wife and I are the only ones at home now; she works part-time at the garment factory in town, so I'm handling most of the field work myself. I have to hire help for the heavy jobs because my back isn't what it used to be, and I need to watch my spending.

I keep 5 mu in the wheat-maize double crop and 2.5 mu for kohlrabi. I need the grain for stability — wheat and maize buyers are reliable, and I can't afford to gamble everything on vegetables. But kohlrabi has been bringing in better money per mu the last two years, so I keep that plot going even though it's more labor and water.

For the wheat I planted last October, I laid down a base of 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer and about 5 kg per mu of urea before sowing. Now it's April and the wheat is greening up well. I had a soil test done through the extension station three years ago — showed medium phosphorus, adequate potassium, but the organic matter was on the low side. Based on that and what I saw last year, I'm topdressing 12 kg per mu of urea at jointing stage. That's roughly 5.5 kg of pure N. I was going to do 15 kg, but urea prices are up again this spring, and I need to keep some cash for the maize seed and the kohlrabi irrigation. Twelve kg should get me to about 450 kg per mu if the weather holds — that's a bit less than Old Wang down the road is aiming for, but he's got more labor and I don't want to overextend. I'll irrigate twice more: once right after the topdressing to wash it in, and once at grain filling. The well water is metered now, so each irrigation costs me. Two more is enough if we get normal spring rains.

For the summer maize, I'm planting Zhengdan 958 right after wheat harvest in mid-June. It's a proven hybrid around here — my neighbor tried a new fancy variety last year and got less yield, so I'm sticking with what works. I'll put down 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress with about 10 kg per mu of urea at the big trumpet stage if the plants look like they need it. That gives me about 13 kg N per mu total. I'm budgeting two irrigations — one at tasseling, one at grain filling. If the summer is wet like two years ago, I might skip one, but I'll plan for two. I hire a planter for the maize because that one-week window after wheat harvest is brutal; you miss it and your yield drops 20%.

The kohlrabi bed I tilled in March with a hired rotary tiller. I put down about 1,000 kg per mu of well-rotted manure plus 30 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as base. I transplanted the seedlings two weeks ago. Kohlrabi is picky about water — if it dries out when the bulbs are swelling, you get woody, small heads. I'm planning four irrigations through May and early June, especially as the bulbs size up. I'll watch for diamondback moth and cabbage worms; if I see damage, I'll spray twice with a bio-pesticide the extension agent recommended, otherwise once preventive. I expect about 1,800 kg per mu if the market-grade heads come through.

My total input budget is about 5,200 yuan this season. That's tight, but my wife's factory work brings in steady cash. I'm prioritizing the kohlrabi on water and labor because the return is better, but I won't starve the wheat — that's my food security base. If all goes well, I'll have enough to cover living expenses and maybe replace the pump on my well before it fails completely.
